newsitem.title: USA: China ready to end some trade barriers - NYT.
newsitem.headline: China ready to end some trade barriers - NYT.

text.p: China has told U.S. officials it was willing to end some of its biggest trade barriers in exchange for membership in the World Trade Organisation, the New York Times reported Wednesday.

Citing information from senior officials of the Clinton Administration, the paper said the barriers included laws protecting some of China's state- and military-run industries from foreign competition.
The paper said the offers have so far been conveyed in conversations only and officials were wary of China's willingness to follow through with some of the changes discussed.

"There always has been a dysfunction between what they say and what they put in writing. And for WTO accession, what they put in writing is what counts," the paper quoted Charlene Barshefsky, the acting U.S. trade respresentative, as saying.
Officials involved in the negotiations said China has agreed to eliminate over time the requirement that foreign companies building factories in China export most of their output, the paper reported.

China has also agreed to phase out rules requiring foreign companies to bring large amounts of foreign currency into the country and to include high levels of local content for their goods, the paper said. Additionally, China has agreed to end laws barring many foreign companies from freely trading internally.
